annotations.title: Thou ſhalt not couet.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> It is not the habitual concupiſcence or infirmitie of our nature or ſenſual deſire or inclination to euil, coueting againſt the ſpirit, that is forbidden properly in this precept: but the conſent of our reaſon and minde vnto it, to obey and folow the luſtes thereof, that is a ſinne and prohibited.

annotations.title: That which I worke.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> This being vnderſtood of S. Paul him ſelf or any other iuſt perſon, the ſenſe is, that the fleſh and inferiour part ſtirreth vp diuerſe diſordered motions and paſſions or perturbations againſt the minde, and vpon ſuch a ſoden ſometimes inuadeth the ſame, that before it attēdeth, or reaſon can gather it ſelf to deliberate, mā is in a ſort (though vnvvittingly) entangled. Vvhich as ſoone as it is perceiued, being of the iuſt condemned, reiected, and reſiſted, neuer maketh him a ſinner.

notes.text: Soden inuoluntarie motions are no sinne.

annotations.title: Not that which I will.
annotations.text: [1] He meaneth not, that he can do no good that he willeth or deſireth, or that he is euer forced to do that which his will agreeth not vnto: but that by reaſon of the forcibleneſſe of concupiſcence, whereof he can not rid him ſelf during life, he can not accompliſh all the deſires of his ſpirit and minde, according as he ſaith to the Galatians, [2] The fleſh coueteth againſt the ſpirit, and the ſpirit againſt the fleſh: that not whatſoeuer you vvill, you can do.

notes.text: Concupiscence taketh not away free wil.

annotations.title: Not the good vvhich I vvill.
annotations.text: [1] So may the iuſt alſo be forced by the rage of concupiſcence or ſenſual appetite, to do or ſuffer many things in his inferiour part or external members, which his will conſenteth not vnto. And ſo long it is ſo farre from ſinne, that (as [2] S. Auguſtine ſaith) he neede neuer ſay to God, forgiue vs our ſinnes, for the ſame. for, ſinne is voluntarie, and ſo be not theſe paſſions.

notes.text: Sinne is voluntarie, and otherwise it is no sinne.

annotations.title: Which I will not.
annotations.text: It maketh not any thing againſt free vvill that the Apoſtle ſaith, that good men do or ſuffer ſometimes in their bodies, that vvhich the will agreeth not vnto: but it proueth plainely free wil. becauſe the proper act thereof, that is, to vvill or nill, to conſent or diſſent, is euer (as you may ſee here) free in it ſelf: though there may be internal or external force to ſtay the members of a man, that they obey not in euery act, that vvhich the vvill commaundeth or preſcribeth. And therfore that is neuer imputed to mā vvhich he doth in his external or internal faculties, vvhen vvil concurreth not. Yea afterward (v, 20) the Apoſtle ſaith, Non ego operor, man doeth not that which is not done by his wil: which doth moſt euidently proue free vvill.

annotations.title: With the minde, vvith the fleſh.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Nothing done by concupiſcence (which the Apoſtle here calleth ſinne) whereunto the ſpirit, reaſon, or minde of man conſenteth not, can make him guilty before God. Neither can the motions of the fleſh in a iuſt man euer any whit defile the operatiōs of his ſpirit, as the Lutherans do hold: but make them often more meritorious, for the continual combat that he hath with them. for it is plaine that the operations of the fleſh and of the ſpirit do not concurre together to make one acte, as they imagine: the Apoſtle concluding cleane contrarie, That in minde he ſerueth the Law of God, in fleſh the law of ſinne, that is to ſay, concupiſcence.

notes.text: Concupiscence defileth not a iust mans actiōs as the Lutherās say.
